name: Freya Quinn

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We're independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we don't sell or campaign. Your answers are confidential, including the parts you wouldn't say at work. What is a normal day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead three renewal clerks in the property-services arm of a large company. We send commercial tenants new terms and arrange access cards so a business can open its door on Monday. I have a bachelor's degree and only moved into this junior lead post this year; I still ask an older colleague about unusual lease clauses. I use an AI drafting tool now and then, but I check the address and card date myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who is at home when you put the lease files down?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58 and live with my partner Ellis, who works paid shifts in a bakery. Our daughter and son are grown and live elsewhere. We have a small mortgage, lower pay for this kind of manager job and only two weeks of expenses saved after dental work; few similar posts are nearby. Retirement is in sight, but we have not checked what either pension would actually pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A modest drafting tool would save us some envelope work, but a tenant still needs a working access card on moving day. Ellis's bakery hours have dropped since the café next door closed, so our household is tight even without new AI. We have two weeks of expenses left in cash after a dental bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my three renewal clerks to check the unit number and delivery date on each letter. I'd tell tenants to call our desk if a card has not arrived, not just wait for a text reply. I use a draft tool occasionally, but I would not let it decide who can enter a building.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm still learning the lease exceptions after being moved into this junior lead post, and I know the experienced leads catch things I miss. My pay is low for the title and there are few comparable offices nearby. With Ellis's bakery shifts cut and a small mortgage due monthly, I already worry about the bank account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll compare the five returned renewal letters with the unit register and phone each tenant before their card expires. Through the first plateau year I'll keep using the current draft tool only for wording after checking the address myself. I'll cancel our paid film subscription for three months and put that 18 monthly toward the electricity bill while Ellis's hours are down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our bills, though the software itself is hardly the reason. The returned envelope is what I see when I close my eyes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened with the returned envelope?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A renewal for unit 24 went to unit 42, and the tenant could not enter on a Sunday. A caretaker opened the door after I found the error, but she had waited outside with shopping. A swapped unit number can leave a person on the pavement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Have your grown children offered help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter lives two hours away and our son rents with friends. They phone, but neither has offered to pay our mortgage, and I have not asked. Ellis and I would talk before asking them for anything.

say: I'd tell clerks to check **unit numbers** before renewal letters leave.
I'd tell tenants to call the **human desk** when cards fail.
think: My **junior lead pay** and Ellis's reduced bakery hours already squeeze the mortgage.
Two weeks cash and few local offices leave **little room for error**.
do: Check **five returned letters** against unit records and call tenants this week.
Keep the **current draft tool** under address review.
Cancel the **film subscription** for three months and use 18 monthly for electricity.
feel: I feel **anxious** about bills and returned letters.
S0.quote: A swapped unit number can leave a person on the pavement.
fieldNote: A unit-number error left a tenant **locked outside** with shopping.
The film subscription cut follows **lost bakery hours**, not AI alarm.
She does not count **adult children** as a household income source.

steps.text: Check five returned renewal letters and call affected tenants this week
Cancel film subscription for three months and use 18 monthly for electricity

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing renewals, checking rent changes, booking access cards and answering tenants are nearly all desk tasks. A stronger system could do the ordinary leases and leave fewer clerks. The caretakers still handle doors for now, but my role is the screen and the phone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the company to test late card deliveries before cutting the renewal desk. I'd tell tenants there must be a named person for an incorrect lockout notice. I'd ask the experienced clerks to log every address the pilot gets wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My junior lead post could be the first manager layer removed if one system oversees several buildings. I use AI sometimes for wording, but I do not know how to audit a decision that changes a tenant's access. Ellis's reduced bakery pay and our two-week buffer would make a lost wage hard to absorb.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January I'd ask for a paid month-long pilot on closed renewal files, with the access manager checking card dates and the director approving the trial. If it catches the unit 24 error and both approve the result, I'd learn the new audit screen on paid time with a trained clerk, then use the tool for routine draft notices only after the director approves rollout and a human checks addresses. I'd apply for posted local contract-admin jobs after checking wages and bus hours, staying here until a signed offer with Ellis's confirmed pay covers mortgage, food and medicine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my post. I can learn a tested screen, but that does not make three desks into six jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the address in the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The access manager has the card log and a trained renewal clerk has the lease file. Both must point to the same unit before a notice goes live. A tidy notice sent to the wrong door is still wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pilot is not approved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I keep the old address check and the phone line. I would ask for a written staffing answer, but I would not run a live trial on my own. Paid time matters because our team is already covering absences.

say: I'd ask for a **late-card pilot** before desk cuts are put into a staffing plan.
I'd demand a **named lockout contact** for tenants with an incorrect notice.
think: My **junior lead post** could disappear as desks combine.
Ellis's reduced pay and two weeks cash make **my wage vital**.
do: Request **paid pilot** with access-manager checks and director approval; learn audit screen with trained clerk on paid time after both approve results.
Use **routine AI draft notices** only after successful pilot, director rollout approval and human address checks.
Apply for **posted local contract jobs** with viable pay and bus hours; leave after affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my job despite willingness to learn.
S1.quote: A tidy notice sent to the wrong door is still wrong.
fieldNote: Her **occasional AI drafts** do not equal skill at access decisions.
A pilot requires **director approval** and card-log checks.
She separates an **application** from leaving for a signed affordable offer.

steps.text: Request paid closed-renewal pilot only with access manager checks and director approval
Learn audit screen with paid trained-clerk instruction only after access manager and director approve successful pilot
Use AI draft renewal notices only after successful pilot, director rollout approval and human address checks
Apply for contract jobs with viable pay and bus hours; leave only after affordable signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 full AGI could write and check every lease, issue card instructions and answer tenant complaints better than our desk. My renewal role might vanish; even another contract office would face the same thinking AI. Caretakers still fix a physical lock until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I have never repaired one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the clerks to request written notice terms and dates. I'd tell Ellis we should stop the planned weekend trip before booking a room. I'd tell tenants to save the access-card number and keep a way to contest an automatic lockout.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior lead wage to end if AGI handles renewals. Ellis's bakery income has already fallen, and two weeks cash would not carry the mortgage through a search; I would lie awake doing that sum. I could learn a tool quickly enough to help now, but that would not make the desk necessary in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd request written notice and severance terms from human resources and cancel the weekend-trip plan before we pay for a room. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my wage ends, I'd apply for posted local work only after checking the duties, bus journey and wage; I'd accept only a signed offer whose pay with Ellis's confirmed bakery hours covers mortgage, food and medicine. I'd check public-help eligibility and apply only if we qualify, asking the lender about a payment arrangement before missing the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. Two weeks of money is no bridge between a closed desk and a new wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you work as a caretaker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can change the batteries in our doorbell, but I do not know commercial locks or safety rules. I would need a real paid opening and training before relying on that work, and robots that can do physical repairs arrive around 2031. I would not put our mortgage on a job I have not seen posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children take you in?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter and son are adults with their own housing costs. If we needed a one-off place to stay, I would ask whether either could offer it and respect a no. I would not list their rooms as our emergency fund.

say: I'd ask for **written notice terms** for the renewal team.
I'd tell tenants to keep **access-card records** for disputes.
think: I expect my **junior lead wage** to end by 2028.
Ellis's reduced bakery pay and two weeks cash cannot cover **the mortgage** through a long job search.
do: Request **written severance terms** and cancel the unbooked weekend trip now.
Apply for **posted local work** only after duty, bus and wage checks; accept signed offer covering family bills.
Check **public-help eligibility** before applying if the desk ends.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by a likely lost wage and two-week reserve.
S2.quote: Two weeks of money is no bridge between a closed desk and a new wage.
fieldNote: She refuses to claim **caretaker skill** because she can change a home doorbell battery.
A physical lock role still faces **2031 robots**, while lease decisions face AGI in 2028.
She would **ask family** about a one-off stay but rely on it only if offered; public aid requires eligibility.

steps.text: Cancel unbooked weekend trip before paying for a room
Apply for local jobs after duty, bus and wage checks; accept only affordable signed offer
Check public-help eligibility and apply only if household qualifies

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives us a chance to rebuild cash while I still have the renewal wage. Lease checking and tenant replies face AGI in 2031; physical lock repairs face capable robots around 2034. I can learn a new screen in the meantime, but I won't claim it keeps a junior lead post alive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for a dated staffing plan and paid instruction on any new tool. I'd tell Ellis we should see actual pension figures before talking about fewer hours. I'd tell tenants a wrong lockout still needs a phone call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep the wage until 2031, and that is our best chance to build more than two weeks in cash. I don't know our pension income or whether I could stop work at sixty-three. A nearby contract role might pay less, and its documents face the same AGI date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I'd ask the pension provider for my eligibility date and monthly estimate, then compare it with mortgage, food and medicine. I'd save 30 weekly only if my wage and Ellis's paid shifts cover those bills, aiming for one month cash before anything else. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd apply for posted nearby work with workable bus hours only if the wage with Ellis's confirmed pay covers essentials; I'd leave my current job only after a signed offer or verified pension income that truly covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but having five years to check the statements helps. A pension figure on paper cannot take the place of a bank deposit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pension estimate is poor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep working if there is paid work I can do. I would not tell Ellis to cut hours based on an estimate. We would keep the bus pass paid before a leisure trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your daughter help with the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask only after Ellis and I have looked at our own numbers. Our daughter has rent and a job of her own. If she offers a one-off loan we would agree repayment, but I would not assume it.

say: I'd ask for a **dated staffing plan** and paid instruction.
I'd tell Ellis to wait for **real pension figures** before fewer hours.
think: My renewal wage may last until 2031, giving us **cash-building time**.
I cannot stop work at sixty-three without **known pension income**.
do: Request **pension eligibility and amount** in 2027 and compare with essentials.
Save **30 weekly** only while both paid incomes cover mortgage, food and medicine.
Apply for **posted bus-accessible work** after 2031 only with affordable combined pay; leave after signed offer or sufficient pension.
feel: I feel **anxious** about an unknown pension and exposed wage.
S3.quote: A pension figure on paper cannot take the place of a bank deposit.
fieldNote: She waits for **actual pension eligibility**, not an assumed retirement date.
The 30 weekly cash transfer needs **two paid incomes** covering essentials.
An adult daughter's loan would require **her offer** and agreed repayment.

steps.text: Request written pension eligibility and monthly estimate in 2027
Save 30 weekly only while both paid incomes cover mortgage, food and medicine
Apply for posted bus-accessible jobs with affordable pay; leave after signed offer or verified sufficient pension

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty-eight in 2036, and our grown children would have their own lives. I don't know whether the mortgage would be gone or what pension amount we would have. Renewal decisions face AGI in 2036, and capable robots could handle physical lock repairs around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the company to give older staff written transition dates. I'd tell Ellis we should check the mortgage balance and pension letters each year. I'd tell tenants where to report a wrong access decision even if a system wrote it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade might let us save and pay down the mortgage if both incomes hold, but we start with only two weeks cash. I would consider fewer hours only if a real pension and a paid part-time post together cover our bills. I don't expect a junior lead title to shield me from AGI in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'd ask the pension provider for written eligibility and amount, then review it with Ellis against mortgage, food and medicine. I'd transfer 45 weekly to cash only after those bills are paid from confirmed wages, stopping if Ellis's bakery shifts fall. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, I'd accept a posted part-time contract job only if its wage with verified pension income and Ellis's confirmed pay covers essentials; I would cut my hours only after a signed offer and actual pension eligibility, otherwise keep seeking full paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about starting the decade with so little, though I can use the years to prepare. I want a statement with dates and amounts, not a birthday card from the company.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no part-time job appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would not cut hours on purpose. I would keep full paid work if it exists and seek another posted role if this one ends. A part-time job on my wish list does not pay the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children help you retire?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They may visit and share a meal, but their wages are their own. Ellis and I would ask them about a one-off emergency only if we needed it, and accept their answer. I will not call their future pay my pension.

say: I'd ask for **written transition dates** for older staff.
I'd tell Ellis to compare **pension and mortgage** yearly.
think: Fewer hours require **real pension** and paid work covering bills.
A junior lead title cannot shield me from **2036 AGI**.
do: Request **pension eligibility and amount** this winter and compare with mortgage costs.
Save **45 weekly** only after bills from confirmed wages, stopping if Ellis's shifts fall.
Take **posted part-time work** after 2036 only with signed offer, pension eligibility and affordable combined pay; otherwise seek full paid work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about thin cash despite time to prepare.
S4.quote: A part-time job on my wish list does not pay the mortgage.
fieldNote: She does not assume **age alone** grants a usable pension.
Her part-time plan needs **actual eligibility**, signed work and affordable combined income.
She will not count **adult children's wages** toward retirement.

steps.text: Request written pension eligibility and monthly amount; compare with mortgage, food and medicine
Save 45 weekly only after bills from confirmed wages; stop if Ellis’s shifts fall
Take posted part-time after 2036 only if signed offer, pension eligible and combined pay covers essentials
Seek full paid work if no viable part-time offer or pension income

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. My renewal wage could end at sixty while Ellis's bakery shifts are already reduced and our cash covers only two weeks. Written notice, a real job whose wages cover the mortgage, and verified support eligibility would help. I also need an honest pension statement, not an assumed retirement age.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the tenant who waited outside with shopping whether a perfect renewal letter helped. The wrong access card still kept the commercial tenant on the pavement. I want someone able to answer the phone when the number on the door is wrong.

headlineQuote: The wrong access card still kept the commercial tenant on the pavement.
portrait: Freya, **58**, recently became junior lead of three commercial-property renewal clerks and holds a bachelor's degree.
She uses AI **occasionally for drafts** but still learns unusual lease clauses from an older colleague.
Low pay, Ellis's reduced bakery hours, a small mortgage and **two weeks cash** limit her choices.
She wants **real pension figures** before considering fewer hours and does not count grown children's wages.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her renewal wage when the household has only two weeks saved.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice**, verified support eligibility and a paid job covering mortgage costs.
She needs an **honest pension statement** before any retirement decision.
